topic: Mastering 3D Linear Transformations: From Vectors to Visuals

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: The Basis of 3D Space
sections.content: Briefly define a 3D vector [x, y, z] and the standard basis vectors: î (1,0,0), ĵ (0,1,0), and k̂ (0,0,1). Emphasize that any vector is a linear combination of these basis vectors.
sections.example: Visualizing a 3D character model as a collection of points in space anchored to the î, ĵ, and k̂ axes.

sections.title: Defining the Transformation Matrix
sections.content: Introduce the 3x3 matrix as a 'transformation machine.' Explain that the columns of the matrix represent the new positions of î, ĵ, and k̂ after the transformation.
sections.example: An animation showing a 'Basis Robot' with arms pointing along x, y, and z axes rotating and stretching into new positions, creating a transformation matrix.

sections.title: Core Transformations: Scaling and Rotation
sections.content: Demonstrate how diagonal elements control scaling (stretching space) and off-diagonal elements control shear/rotation. Explain the preservation of origin and straight lines.
sections.example: An elephant character being 'stretched' along the z-axis (scaling) or 'tilted' (shearing) while maintaining its proportions.

sections.title: Composition: Matrix Multiplication
sections.content: Explain that applying two transformations in sequence is equivalent to multiplying their matrices (A * B). Remind that order matters (non-commutative property).
sections.example: A gaming device character: First apply a 'Rotate' matrix, then a 'Scale' matrix. Show how the order of operations changes the final pose of the character.

sections.title: Summary and Geometric Intuition
sections.content: Recap: A matrix is just a re-mapping of 3D space. Keep the mental model: 'Where did the basis vectors land?' to understand any 3D transformation.
sections.example: A quick-fire montage: A 3D object moving through various complex transformations, showing how the matrix columns dictate the final orientation.
